Leathern
LETH-ern
adj. (made of leather)
From leather with the old adjectival ending -en, as in wooden and golden. The Authorized Version uses it once, of the girdle John the Baptist wore about his loins.

Biblical Definition

And the same John had his raiment of camel's hair, and a leathern girdle about his loins; and his meat was locusts and wild honey. The description is not incidental colour. It is a deliberate quotation of Elijah, whom the men of Ahaziah described as an hairy man, girt with a girdle of leather about his loins, and it announced John's office before he opened his mouth: the prophet promised in Malachi, come in the spirit and power of Elias. Everything about the clothing says wilderness rather than court. The Lord made the contrast himself: What went ye out into the wilderness to see? A reed shaken with the wind? But what went ye out for to see? A man clothed in soft raiment? behold, they that wear soft clothing are in kings' houses. John was not in a king's house; he was eventually in a king's prison, for telling that king the truth about his brother's wife. His message was four words long and it has never been improved: Repent ye: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand. And the Lord's verdict on him is the highest given to any man born of woman, with a sting in its tail for the least in the kingdom.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828): made of leather; consisting of leather; in Scripture, the girdle of John the Baptist, worn after the manner of Elijah.

expand to see more

LEATHERN, a. Made of leather; consisting of leather; as a leathern purse.

LEATHER, n. The skin of an animal dressed and prepared for use.

GIRDLE, n. A band or belt; something drawn round the waist of a person and tied or buckled.

RAIMENT, n. Clothing in general; vestments; vesture; garments.

FORERUNNER, n. A messenger sent before to give notice of the approach of another.

Key Scripture

Mat 3:4 — "And the same John had his raiment of camel's hair, and a leathern girdle about his loins; and his meat was locusts and wild honey."

Mat 3:2 — "And saying, Repent ye: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand."

Mat 11:8 — "But what went ye out for to see? A man clothed in soft raiment? behold, they that wear soft clothing are in kings' houses."

Mat 11:11 — "Verily I say unto you, Among them that are born of women there hath not risen a greater than John the Baptist: notwithstanding he that is least in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he."

Modern Corruption

Repentance is softened into a change of perspective or a general spiritual openness, and the preacher who names sin is judged harsh; John's office, dress, diet and message were all a standing refusal of that softening.

expand to see more

John's preaching is the pattern the dictionary keeps for the ministry of repentance. He called the religious leaders a generation of vipers and asked who had warned them to flee from the wrath to come; he told the multitudes to bring forth fruits meet for repentance; he gave the publicans and the soldiers specific, concrete instructions about money and violence; and he told Herod that it was not lawful for him to have his brother's wife, which cost him his head. Repentance in Scripture is a turning that shows, with fruit attached, and no part of John's ministry supports the idea that naming a particular sin to a particular man is unloving.

The clothing carries the argument silently. Soft raiment belongs in kings' houses; camel's hair and a leathern girdle belong in the wilderness where a man has nothing to lose and no patron to please. A ministry that has arranged its comforts inside the palace will find it very difficult to say the sentence John said to Herod. And yet the Lord's verdict keeps even John in proportion: he that is least in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he — not because John was small, but because the kingdom he announced is that great.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Greek dermatinos (G1193), made of skin or leather; zone (G2223), a girdle or belt; metanoeo (G3340), to repent, to change the mind.

Greek dermatinos (G1193) — made of hide or leather; the leathern girdle of Matthew 3:4.

Greek zone (G2223) — a belt or girdle worn about the loins.

Greek endyma (G1742) — a garment, raiment; his raiment of camel's hair.

Greek metanoeo (G3340) — to change the mind, to repent; Repent ye.

Greek malakos (G3120) — soft, delicate; a man clothed in soft raiment.

Usage

"“a leathern girdle about his loins” — the single occurrence, of John the Baptist."

"“they that wear soft clothing are in kings' houses” — the contrast the Lord drew."

"“Repent ye: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand” — the message the dress announced."
